stations.title: One scene, three bodies
stations.concept: The same Cabinet exists as a rendering, as Turtle text and as a graph of triples.
stations.misconception: "The 3D view is the scene; the RDF is a side export."
stations.story: Everything you see on the floor of this room also exists as text and as a graph. The X3D file was translated, with the Consortium stylesheet, into Turtle: short sentences about every node. Count them: each one is a fact you can ask about, and every node they describe has a bead floating above its object.

stations.title: A triple is a sentence
stations.concept: Subject, predicate, object: one fact. A node is described by all triples with it as subject.
stations.misconception: "A node is a row in a table with fixed columns."
stations.story: Gilt is the gold Material on the first plinth. In the graph it is a subject with a handful of predicates: its type, its parent, its DEF name and its colour. Ask for everything said about Gilt and you get one row per sentence.

stations.title: IRIs, not labels
stations.concept: A property is an IRI. The XML attribute name geometry is not the RDF property x3do:hasGeometry.
stations.misconception: "If I type the field name I see in the X3D file, the query will find it."
stations.story: In X3D the Box sits in the Shape's geometry field. In the twin, that link is the property x3do:hasGeometry, an exact IRI. A query that guesses x3do:geometry is perfectly legal and finds nothing: SPARQL never complains about a property nobody uses.

stations.title: Instance and class
stations.concept: rdf:type links an individual in the scene to a class in the ontology. Classes live in the sky, instances on the floor.
stations.misconception: "The Spinner in my scene is a kind of Transform, so it is a subclass."
stations.story: The Spinner is one particular Transform: an instance. Transform itself is a class in the X3D Ontology, and it has ancestors of its own. The plumb line from the Spinner's bead up to the dome is rdf:type; the lines along the dome are rdfs:subClassOf.

stations.title: DEF is identity, USE is sameAs
stations.concept: A DEF name becomes the node's IRI. In X3D a USE is not a copy: it is the same node appearing a second time. The stylesheet gives each USE its own IRI (Gilt-USE-1) and states owl:sameAs Gilt: two names, one thing. OWL makes no unique-name assumption, so two IRIs may denote one node unless owl:differentFrom says otherwise; sameAs says so explicitly. Plain SPARQL does not merge them; follow owl:sameAs yourself (T5.5).
stations.misconception: "Three gold orbs means three gold Materials."
stations.story: The three orbs on the first plinth share one Material, DEF'd once as Gilt and USE'd twice. The twin gives the two USE references their own IRIs and ties them to the DEF with owl:sameAs: two names for one node. The six other plinths are the same trick: one PlinthGroup, USE'd six times.

stations.title: Unnamed nodes get positional names
stations.concept: A node without DEF is named by its position (Appearance_2_12_3_1_1_1). Insert one node earlier and those names shift.
stations.misconception: "Every node keeps its identity across edits."
stations.story: Nodes you did not name still need an IRI, so the stylesheet spells out their path: child 12 of the Scene, child 3 of that, and so on. Add a single light at the top of the Scene and the positional names below it shift, while every DEF'd node keeps its IRI. Worse than a vanished name is a survivor: some positional IRIs exist in both versions but now name a different node (a ROUTE that was Spin's now leaves the Clock; counted below). DEF what matters.

stations.title: Colours are lists
stations.concept: An SFColor becomes an rdf:List: a chain of rdf:first / rdf:rest cells, read by position.
stations.misconception: "diffuseColor is one value I can compare."
stations.story: The Ruby prism's colour is three numbers. In RDF that is a little linked list: the first cell holds red, the rest of the list holds green and blue. To read the colour you walk the chain, and the chain cells are some of the most common triples in the whole twin.

stations.title: FILTER on a computed brightness
stations.concept: BIND computes a value (a brightness from the colour list, BT.709 weights on the stored numbers); FILTER keeps rows; ORDER BY sorts them.
stations.misconception: "SPARQL can only match what is literally stored."
stations.story: No triple says how bright a Material looks. The Pearl prism and the plaque top the list; the glowing Ember is too dark in diffuse terms to pass.

# Semantic Twin Lab: RDFS entailment rules used by the Chimera and launder stations (shown with a warning).
# Rules rdfs2 (domain), rdfs3 (range), rdfs5/rdfs7 (subPropertyOf), rdfs9/rdfs11 (subClassOf). No axiomatic triples,
# no rdfs4 (everything is a Resource), so counts compare to owlrl by the rdf:type triples on IRI subjects only.
# Multiple rdfs:domain (or rdfs:range) values mean INTERSECTION: a subject gets every domain class at once.
# Run with a derivation budget (e.g. new N3.Reasoner(store, { maxDerivations: 2e6 })).
@prefix rdf:  <http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#> .
@prefix rdfs: <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#> .

{ ?p rdfs:domain ?c . ?s ?p ?o . } => { ?s rdf:type ?c . } .
{ ?p rdfs:range ?c . ?s ?p ?o . } => { ?o rdf:type ?c . } .
{ ?p rdfs:subPropertyOf ?q . ?s ?p ?o . } => { ?s ?q ?o . } .
{ ?p rdfs:subPropertyOf ?q . ?q rdfs:subPropertyOf ?r . } => { ?p rdfs:subPropertyOf ?r . } .
{ ?s rdf:type ?a . ?a rdfs:subClassOf ?b . } => { ?s rdf:type ?b . } .
{ ?a rdfs:subClassOf ?b . ?b rdfs:subClassOf ?c . } => { ?a rdfs:subClassOf ?c . } .

stations.title: The NURBS Box
stations.concept: Pooled rdfs:range values: every range of hasGeometry is applied to every geometry node.
stations.misconception: "rdfs:range checks that the value is the right kind."
stations.story: The Ruby prism's Box has no DEF, but it has a size, and x3do:size is declared for many node types: RDFS makes the Box a FontStyle, a ProximitySensor and a Rectangle2D as well. hasGeometry lists three ranges, and RDFS gives the Box all three: it becomes a parametric (NURBS) geometry node and an N-body collidable node too. stations.title: OWL is not a schema
stations.concept: OWL objects only to what it can prove inconsistent. This ontology declares no disjointness, cardinality or functional-property axioms (census below), so almost nothing a scene states can be inconsistent: a Box can also be a Transform.
stations.misconception: "The ontology will tell me a Box cannot also be a Transform."
stations.story: The X3D Ontology 4.1 declares no disjoint classes, no cardinalities and no functional properties. So a reasoner will happily let one node be a Box and a Transform at once: consistent, open world. Counting the disjointness axioms takes one line.

stations.concept: A NodeShape targets a class and constrains its nodes; a result names the focus node, severity and message. In SHACL, sh:conforms is false as soon as there is any result, Warning and Info included; severity is a label on the result. x3d_mcp's verdict uses its own gate policy: conforms is false only for a Violation, and warnings are counted, not failed.

stations.title: Map, not gate
stations.concept: The ontology proposes where a node may go; the X3DUOM table and the XSD decide. They do not agree.
stations.misconception: "If the ontology allows a placement, it is legal X3D."
stations.story: Ask the ontology where a Box may be placed and it proposes a list of parent fields. The X3D object model's own placement table lists fewer, and the XSD accepts fewer still. The ontology proposes, shapes dispose, the validator gates. (Map counts use named ranges only: owl:unionOf ranges are not expanded, hence isIRI(?range).)

stations.title: Two validators disagree
stations.concept: Graph roles matter: shacl-engine 1.1.3 reads the class hierarchy from the SHAPES graph, pyshacl from the data graph. SHACL 1.0 defines "SHACL instance" (used by sh:class and sh:targetClass) through rdf:type/rdfs:subClassOf* in the data graph, so pyshacl follows the Recommendation and shacl-engine 1.1.3 departs from it. The SHACL 1.2 Core editors' draft adds a subClassOfInShapesGraph parameter; that is draft, not standard.
stations.misconception: "Any SHACL engine gives the same answer."
stations.story: Run S7 on the clean Cabinet. pyshacl finds the subclass axioms in the data graph and passes everything. shacl-engine looks for them in the shapes graph, finds none, and reports every child as a violation until the subClassOf triples are copied across. The page always applies that copy; the unfixed count is shown so you can see why.

"""cabinet-twin: one SPARQL query over the Cabinet's Turtle twin, served as an MCP tool (FastMCP, stdio)."""
import json, pathlib
import rdflib
from mcp.server.fastmcp import FastMCP

TWIN = rdflib.Graph().parse(pathlib.Path(__file__).parent.parent / "ttl" / "cabinet.ttl")
QUERY = """PREFIX x3do: <https://www.web3d.org/specifications/X3dOntology4.1#>
PREFIX rdf: <http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#>
SELECT ?material ?Y WHERE {
  ?material a x3do:Material ; x3do:diffuseColor ?c .
  ?c rdf:first ?r ; rdf:rest/rdf:first ?g ; rdf:rest/rdf:rest/rdf:first ?b .
  BIND(0.2126 * ?r + 0.7152 * ?g + 0.0722 * ?b AS ?Y)
  FILTER(?Y > ?min)
} ORDER BY DESC(?Y)"""
mcp = FastMCP("cabinet-twin")


@mcp.tool()
def bright_materials(min_luminance: float = 0.2) -> str:
    """Materials in the Cabinet whose diffuseColor is brighter than min_luminance (relative luminance 0..1)."""
    rows = TWIN.query(QUERY, initBindings={"min": rdflib.Literal(min_luminance)})
    return json.dumps([{"material": m.split("#")[1], "Y": round(float(y), 4)} for m, y in rows])


if __name__ == "__main__":
    mcp.run()  # stdio transport: list this file in an MCP client's server configuration

Wrap it: FastMCP("cabinet-twin") and one @mcp.tool() function whose arguments become the tool's input schema and whose docstring is what the LLM reads.
Bind the parameter with initBindings instead of pasting it into the query text (no injection).
Run it over stdio (python wire_your_own_tool.py) and list it in an MCP client's server configuration.
Test it like the lab did: list_tools, call_tool, compare the rows with the oracle.

stations.title: One graph instructs and checks
stations.concept: SHACL 1.2 (editors' draft) adds sh:agentInstruction: the same shapes that check an agent can tell it the rule first.
stations.misconception: "Instructions and validation are separate documents that drift apart."
stations.story: Lab shapes and the bundled x3d-core shapes carry an sh:agentInstruction sentence. A server can hand those sentences to the model before it writes, then validate with the very same shapes after; the semantic_audit prompt does the first half. sh:agentInstruction is from the SHACL 1.2 Core editors' draft; SHACL 1.0 engines ignore it.
